article.title: Forma corta del participio pasivo
article.part: Participios y deeprichastiya — Причастия и деепричастия

claims.sectionKey: La forma corta del participio pasivo
claims.summary: The short form of the passive participle is used primarily to indicate that a person or thing has received an action or is in the resulting state from that action.

The short form agrees with the subject in gender and number, but does not decline by case like the long form. It often omits the verb 'to be' in present tense and can include the agent in instrumental case.

The same short form can express either a passive voice of an event or a resulting state, depending on the context. The presence of an agent, temporal expressions, and the aspect of the verb help distinguish between these.
